issues.title: A cheaper model with a smarter adviser on call
issues.intro: Nothing new has been published since yesterday: no Claude Code release, no Anthropic blog post, nothing from Simon Willison. So this issue catches up on the past week of Claude Platform release notes, which earlier issues skipped. It's for people building on the API.
tldr: The advisor tool lets a cheaper model do the work and ask a smarter one for the plan, so most tokens are billed at the cheaper rate.
Fast mode on Fable 5.2 writes up to 2.5x faster at double the price. It doesn't start answering any sooner.
On Fable 5.2, only ever add to a conversation. Editing the system prompt, tools or an earlier message can now get the request rejected.

items.headline: The advisor tool: executor does the work, advisor makes the plan
items.summary: The advisor tool (beta) lets a faster, lower-cost executor model consult a higher-intelligence advisor model in the middle of a task. The advisor reads the whole conversation and returns a plan or a course correction, then the executor carries on. Anthropic's docs say that for coding, a Sonnet executor at medium effort with an Opus advisor is comparable to Sonnet at default effort, at lower cost. What changed with Fable 5.2: a Fable 5.2 executor only accepts Fable 5.2 or Mythos 5.2 as its advisor, and every executor accepts Fable 5.2 as its advisor.
items.try: Use it for long multi-step work where most turns are mechanical. It's a weak fit for single-turn questions. Each advisor call is billed at the advisor's rate, so cap them with max_uses, and turn on advisor caching only when you expect three or more calls in a conversation.

items.headline: Fast mode comes to Fable 5.2
items.summary: Set speed: "fast" on a Messages API request and Fable 5.2 produces up to 2.5x more output tokens per second, at $16 in and $80 out per million tokens, double the standard price. It's the same model with no change in intelligence. The gain is in how fast the answer is written, not in time to first token. Prompt caching multipliers apply on top of the fast price.
items.try: Pay for it where a person is waiting on a long answer. Leave it off for background jobs nobody is watching.

items.headline: Fable 5.2 enforces the prefix check for everyone
items.summary: On Fable 5.2, each thinking block is tied to what came before it: the system prompt, the tools and every earlier message. If your code edits any of those and then sends a later thinking block back, the request returns a 400 error. Switching models is safe: keep sending the whole conversation, and blocks the new model can't read are dropped for that request and not billed. No other model reads Fable 5.2's thinking blocks, so a move to Opus 5.5 continues without that reasoning.
items.try: Treat conversation history as append-only and send assistant turns back exactly as the API returned them. Don't keep a separate history per model. Before switching an existing app to Fable 5.2, check whether it edits the prefix.

quickHits.text: Self-hosted Claude Managed Agents: run the whole service on your own infrastructure and keep agents, sessions and history there. Access is by request through your Anthropic account team.
Dreams (research preview) in Managed Agents now supports Fable 5.2.
Fable 5.2 uses the new computer_toolset_20260801 for computer use. Declaring the older computer_20251124 tool returns a 400 error everywhere except Amazon Bedrock.
Text from Opus 4.6, Opus 4.5, Sonnet 4.5 and Haiku 4.5 now carries Anthropic's text watermark on supported platforms. A non-default temperature, top_p or top_k might leave it off.

issues.title: Compaction in plan mode just got pricier
issues.intro: A quiet day. Nothing new from Anthropic's blogs or from Simon Willison, so this issue is all Claude Code 2.1.326, which is mostly safety tightening with a few changes that touch your token bill.
tldr: With opusplan, automatic compaction in plan mode now runs on Opus, so it can cost more.
/update-config now uses about 13,000 tokens of context, down from 93,000.
Code Mode can now be turned on alongside agent teams.
Hooks and wildcard allow rules behave more strictly. Check yours after updating.

items.headline: Plan-mode compaction now uses the model that's answering you
items.summary: Automatic compaction in plan mode now runs on the model answering you. If you use opusplan, that's Opus, so the changelog warns it can cost more. Compaction reads the whole conversation to summarise it, which makes it one of the larger requests in a long session.
items.try: If you plan with opusplan, run /clear before starting an unrelated task so there's less history for a plan-mode compaction to summarise.

items.headline: /update-config is about 7x lighter
items.summary: The built-in /update-config command now uses about 13,000 tokens of context instead of 93,000, and a rejected settings edit quotes only the settings that changed.
items.try: Nothing to do except update. It's a reminder that slash commands load context too, and /usage shows what each one costs you.

items.headline: Code Mode now works with agent teams
items.summary: Until now you couldn't start Code Mode with agent teams enabled. From 2.1.326 you can, and if you had already turned Code Mode on, sessions with teams enabled now start in it. Its permission checks also got stricter: more sandboxed commands ask or are refused, and the $ shell helper refuses some values with an error.
items.try: Code Mode is still experimental and opt-in. Set CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_CODE_MODE=1 in a terminal session to try it.

items.headline: Stricter hooks and allow rules: check your setup
items.summary: Several enforcement changes could surprise an existing configuration. A hook's "decision": "block" now holds in more cases, so a hook that always prints one may start blocking calls. Auto mode now ignores some wildcard shell allow rules, such as ones that name no program or start with $HOME, and lets its safety check decide instead. Some tool calls in bypass permissions mode now ask for approval, or are denied where nobody can be asked.
items.try: After updating, run a normal task and watch for new blocks or prompts. For unattended runs, test once before trusting the schedule.

quickHits.text: The /claude-api skill now builds agents on Managed Agents by default, unless you want to host the agent loop yourself.
/usage in fullscreen mode now shows your plan limit bars before session cost. /cost still starts with cost.
/doctor now shares findings as it works instead of staying silent until the full report.
A startup warning now flags an --allowedTools, --disallowedTools or --tools entry that doesn't look like a complete rule. Useful for scripts.
Remote Control replies now stream to your phone or browser as they are written.

issues.title: One script instead of twenty round trips
issues.intro: First issue, so this one catches up on the last two weeks from Anthropic. The common thread: load less, do more per step.
tldr: Code Mode (experimental) lets Claude batch many tool calls into one script and read back only what it needs.
Anthropic's advice on subagents: you probably have too many. One loop with skills and tool search is often about 2x faster.
Message threads make long sessions start answering about 35% faster, but they don't save tokens.
For memory, keep the always-loaded part tiny. A wiki plus search beat search alone and saved about 20,000 tokens per question.

items.headline: Code Mode: Claude writes a script instead of calling tools one by one
items.summary: New in Claude Code 2.1.323 behind an opt-in flag. Claude writes a short piece of JavaScript that runs several tool calls, in parallel if it likes, passes one result into the next, and returns only the part it needs to read. Best for repeated edits across many files, searches that need filtering, and independent commands that can run together.
items.try: Set CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_CODE_MODE=1 before starting claude in a terminal. Terminal only for now, and a Code Mode session can only be resumed with Code Mode on.

items.headline: When to fold subagents back into your main agent
items.summary: Anthropic argues many teams split work across too many specialist agents. Details get lost at each handoff and every nested loop adds delay. One customer saw roughly 2x faster runs with a single loop. The replacement is progressive disclosure: skills hold the how-to, tool search keeps tool definitions out of the prompt until needed. Tool choice gets worse past about 30 to 50 loaded tools.
items.try: Keep a subagent only when it runs in parallel, needs a throwaway context for noisy work, or your eval shows the single loop doing worse. Fold in one at a time and re-run the eval.

items.headline: Message threads: send the conversation once
items.summary: A Messages API beta where the server keeps the conversation and each later request sends only the new messages. Median time to first token drops about 35% on requests of 500k to 1M tokens. It's already on by default for most Claude Code users. Token usage and price are unchanged, because Claude still reads the whole conversation.
items.try: If you build on the API, add the thread parameter and handle the 5-minute idle expiry by resending the full conversation.

items.headline: The components of agent memory, and why agents should 'dream'
items.summary: Anthropic lays out memory as layers: raw transcripts, notes, organised wikis, and a small set of notes injected into every session. Dreaming is an offline pass that checks notes against transcripts and reorganises them. On a 350,000-file corpus, wiki plus search scored 61% against 53% for search alone and used about 20,000 fewer tokens per question. Rigid rules such as 'record only failures' made stronger models worse.
items.try: Tell the agent what memory is for instead of giving it a procedure. Store only what it can't look up again, and mark which facts are verified.

items.headline: Building always-on agents
items.summary: A guide to agents that work across many sessions, built from five parts: an event inbox, timers, memory, permissions and an outbox. Each wake-up loads a baseline of system prompt, tool definitions and memory files, so that baseline is where the cost lives.
items.try: Keep the baseline lean and cache it. Before compaction or a fresh session, write anything important to memory.
